topics.title: Reflection and images in a plane mirror

learn.hook: Why is the word AMBULANCE written backwards on the front of an ambulance? A mirror holds the answer!
points: When light falls on a shiny surface and bounces back, it is called reflection. The ray hitting the mirror is the incident ray; the ray bouncing off is the reflected ray.
The normal is a line drawn at 90° to the mirror where the ray strikes it. Angles are measured from the normal.
Law of reflection: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal all lie in the same plane.
A plane mirror forms an image that is erect (upright), the same size as the object, and as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.
The image is virtual (it cannot be caught on a screen) and laterally inverted: left and right appear swapped.

example.q: Think it through: A ray of light makes an angle of 30° with the surface of a plane mirror. What is the angle of reflection?
steps: Angles are measured from the normal, which is at 90° to the mirror.
Angle of reflection = angle of incidence = 60°.

learn.reallife: AMBULANCE is printed in mirror writing so that drivers ahead read it correctly in their rear-view mirrors and make way.

games.title: Mirror magic
items: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
This is the law of reflection.
A plane mirror image can be caught on a screen.
It is a virtual image, so no screen can catch it.
In a plane mirror your right hand appears as the image's left hand.
This swapping of sides is lateral inversion.
A plane mirror makes you look smaller than you are.
The image in a plane mirror is the same size as the object.
Angles of incidence and reflection are measured from the normal.
The normal is the line at 90° to the mirror at the point where the ray strikes.

items.q: Angle of incidence 25°. Angle of reflection, in degrees?
Angle of incidence 45°. Angle of reflection, in degrees?
Ray makes 70° with the mirror surface. Angle of incidence, in degrees?
Ray makes 50° with the mirror surface. Angle of reflection, in degrees?
Ray falls along the normal. Angle of incidence, in degrees?

quiz.q: The angle of incidence is 35°. What is the angle of reflection?
quiz.explain: By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 90° even though the angle is already measured from the normal

quiz.q: A ray makes an angle of 40° with a plane mirror's surface. What is the angle of incidence?
steps: The normal is at 90° to the surface
quiz.explain: The angle of incidence is measured from the normal, not from the mirror surface.
quiz.mistake: Measures the angle from the mirror surface instead of the normal

quiz.q: Raju stands 2 m in front of a plane mirror. How far is he from his image?
steps: The image is 2 m behind the mirror
quiz.explain: The image is as far behind the mirror as he is in front of it.
quiz.mistake: Gives the distance to the mirror instead of to the image

quiz.q: Why is 'AMBULANCE' written in mirror writing on ambulances?
options: So it reads correctly in the rear-view mirror of the vehicle ahead
Because the letters are easier to paint
quiz.explain: A mirror laterally inverts the writing back to normal for the driver ahead.
quiz.mistake: Does not apply lateral inversion to a real situation

quiz.q: Which describes the image in a plane mirror?
quiz.explain: A plane mirror always gives a virtual, upright image of the same size.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up plane mirror images with those of curved mirrors

quiz.q: What is the normal in reflection?
options: The ray that comes from the Sun
A line at 90° to the mirror at the point where the ray strikes
quiz.explain: The normal is a reference line at right angles to the surface, from which both angles are measured.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'normal' means an ordinary ray

quiz.q: A virtual image is one that:
options: Cannot be obtained on a screen
quiz.explain: Rays only seem to come from a virtual image, so a screen cannot catch it.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of a virtual image

quiz.q: A ray of light falls on a mirror along the normal. What is the angle of reflection?
quiz.explain: Along the normal, the angle of incidence is 0°, so the angle of reflection is also 0° and the ray goes straight back.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a ray along the normal makes 90° with the normal

teach.ask: Gappu taps a mirror: There is another Gappu inside! But he raises his left wing when I raise my right. What is going on?
teach.praise: Light bounces off the mirror with equal angles, and the image is virtual with left and right swapped. Hello, mirror me!
teach.nudge: What does light do when it hits a mirror? And what happens to left and right in the image?

learn.hook: Look into a shiny steel spoon. The inside shows you upside down, and the back shows you tiny and upright. One spoon, two kinds of mirrors!
points: Spherical mirrors are curved like part of a hollow ball. A concave mirror curves inward (like the inside of a spoon); a convex mirror bulges outward (like the back of a spoon).
A concave mirror makes an object placed very close to it look bigger, erect and virtual. For a far object it forms an inverted image that is real and can be caught on a screen.
Concave mirrors are used in torches and vehicle headlights (to send out a strong beam), as shaving and dentists' mirrors, and in solar cookers to concentrate sunlight.
A convex mirror always forms an erect, smaller (diminished) and virtual image, and shows a wide area.
Convex mirrors are used as rear-view mirrors in vehicles and at sharp turns on hill roads so drivers can see what is coming.

example.q: Think it through: A dentist holds a small curved mirror close to a tooth and sees a bigger upright image. Which kind of mirror is it?
steps: The image is bigger (enlarged) and upright.
A convex mirror always makes images smaller, so it is not convex.
A concave mirror gives an enlarged, erect image when the object is very close.

learn.reallife: On winding ghat roads in places like Munnar or Shimla, large convex mirrors at bends let drivers see vehicles coming around the corner.

items: Torch reflector

quiz.q: Which mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
quiz.explain: A convex mirror gives an upright image and a wide field of view of the traffic behind.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a concave mirror is used because it magnifies

quiz.q: The image formed by a convex mirror is always:
quiz.explain: Whatever the object's position, a convex mirror gives an erect, diminished, virtual image.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the images of convex and concave mirrors

quiz.q: Which mirror is used in a torch to make a strong beam of light?
quiz.explain: A concave reflector sends the bulb's light out as a strong, nearly parallel beam.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the use of concave reflectors

quiz.q: A shaving mirror makes the face look bigger. It is a:
quiz.explain: With the face close to it, a concave mirror forms an enlarged, erect image.
quiz.mistake: Thinks convex mirrors magnify

quiz.q: The inside of a shiny steel spoon acts as a:
quiz.explain: Its reflecting surface curves inward, like a cave, which is why it is called concave.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the inside and the back of a spoon

quiz.q: Why are convex mirrors placed at sharp bends on hill roads?
options: They show a wide area so drivers can see oncoming vehicles
They light up the road at night
quiz.explain: Convex mirrors give a wider view, helping drivers see around the bend.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the mirror is used to magnify

quiz.q: Which mirror can form a real image that can be caught on a screen?
quiz.explain: A concave mirror forms a real, inverted image of distant objects, like a window, on a screen.
quiz.mistake: Thinks mirrors cannot form real images

quiz.q: Solar cookers use concave mirrors because they:
options: Concentrate sunlight onto a small area
quiz.explain: A concave mirror brings sunlight together to a small area, producing heat for cooking.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that concave mirrors converge light

teach.ask: Gappu looks into a spoon: Inside I am upside down, but on the back I am tiny and upright! Why?
teach.praise: The inside of the spoon is a concave mirror and can flip me upside down; the back is a convex mirror and always makes me small and upright!
teach.nudge: What are the two curved mirrors called? What kind of image does each one make?

topics.title: Lenses and the images they form

learn.hook: Your grandparents' reading glasses, a phone camera and a school microscope all work because of a curved piece of glass called a lens!
points: A lens is a piece of transparent material with at least one curved surface. Light bends (refracts) as it passes through it.
A convex lens is thicker in the middle than at the edges. It brings parallel rays of light together (converging lens).
A convex lens held close to an object gives an enlarged, erect, virtual image: this is a magnifying glass. For a distant object, it forms a real, inverted image on a screen.
A concave lens is thinner in the middle than at the edges. It spreads light rays apart (diverging lens) and always forms an erect, smaller, virtual image.
Lenses are used in spectacles, cameras, microscopes, telescopes and projectors. Safety: never look at the Sun through a lens, and never use a lens to focus sunlight on anything, as it can burn.

example.q: Think it through: Anjali holds a lens between a bright window and a white wall and sees a small, upside-down picture of the window on the wall. Which lens is it?
steps: The image is caught on the wall, so it is a real image.
It is inverted, which happens for a real image from a convex lens.
A concave lens always gives virtual images, which cannot be caught on a wall.

learn.reallife: Jewellers and watch repairers use a convex lens (an eyepiece magnifier) to see tiny details. Spectacles for people who cannot see far clearly use concave lenses.

items.text: A magnifying glass is a ___ lens.
Light bending as it passes through a lens is called ___.

quiz.q: A convex lens is:
options: Thicker in the middle than at the edges
Thinner in the middle than at the edges
quiz.explain: A convex lens bulges outward in the middle.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the shapes of convex and concave lenses

quiz.q: Which lens is used as a magnifying glass?
quiz.explain: Held close to small print, a convex lens gives an enlarged, erect image.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a concave lens magnifies

quiz.q: The image formed by a concave lens is always:
quiz.explain: A concave lens spreads rays apart, so it always gives a small, upright, virtual image.
quiz.mistake: Confuses concave lenses with convex lenses

quiz.q: Which lens can form an image of a distant tree on a screen?
quiz.explain: A convex lens converges light and can form a real, inverted image on a screen.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a concave lens forms real images

quiz.q: The bending of light as it passes from air into glass is called:
quiz.explain: Refraction is the bending of light when it passes from one transparent material to another.
quiz.mistake: Confuses refraction with reflection

quiz.q: A concave lens is called a diverging lens because it:
quiz.explain: Rays passing through a concave lens spread out.
quiz.mistake: Reverses converging and diverging

quiz.q: Why must you never look at the Sun through a lens?
options: The lens can focus strong sunlight and badly damage the eyes
It is only a rule with no reason
quiz.explain: A lens can concentrate sunlight enough to burn, which can seriously harm the eyes.
quiz.mistake: Does not realise lenses concentrate dangerous sunlight

quiz.q: Which of these uses lenses?
quiz.explain: A microscope uses an eyepiece lens and objective lenses. The others use reflecting surfaces.
quiz.mistake: Confuses devices with mirrors and devices with lenses

teach.ask: Gappu peers through Dadi's reading glass: The ant looks huge! What kind of lens is this and how is it different from the other kind?
teach.praise: Dadi's glass is a convex lens, thick in the middle, that makes things bigger. A concave lens is thin in the middle and makes them smaller!
teach.nudge: What is the name of this lens and what is its shape? How is the other lens different?
